questions.q: Which of these is explicitly listed as a red flag for an unsustainable incentive design?
options: Rewards are partly paid from real trading fee revenue
Emissions are capped and taper on a published schedule
The protocol has a long vesting schedule for insiders
No token sink -- nothing removes tokens from circulation to offset new emissions
questions.explain: Having no token sink (burns, lockups, fee payments) to offset new emissions is one of the lesson's listed red flags.

questions.q: What is the key difference between "real yield" and "inflationary yield"?
options: Real yield is always higher than inflationary yield
Real yield is paid from actual protocol revenue; inflationary yield is paid primarily from newly minted tokens
They are the same thing with different names
Inflationary yield is always paid in USDC
questions.explain: Real yield comes from actual revenue (independent of token price); inflationary yield depends on new token issuance holding its value.

questions.q: In the worked comparison, why is Protocol A's 150% APY considered fragile?
options: 150% APY is always a fraud regardless of its source
It is backed entirely by real trading fee revenue
It's backed almost entirely by $15,000,000 in new token issuance against only $50,000 in real revenue
The protocol has no emissions at all
questions.explain: The yield only holds its value as long as the token price survives the weight of $15,000,000/year in new supply -- it's not backed by real revenue.

questions.q: What is a "Ponzi-shaped incentive," as described in this lesson?
options: A design structurally dependent on new deposits to pay existing depositors' yield
Any incentive design that uses token emissions at all
A design that pays 100% of yield from real fees
A governance-only token with no utility function
questions.explain: The lesson describes this shape as structurally identical to a Ponzi scheme, regardless of intent, because it only works while new capital keeps arriving.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the lesson's four principles for sustainable incentive design?
options: Never use any token emissions, even to bootstrap a new protocol
Pay all yield exclusively in newly minted tokens
Avoid tapering emissions so participants aren't surprised
Match lock duration to reward duration
questions.explain: Matching lock duration to reward duration is one of the four principles listed, alongside paying real yield, capping/tapering emissions, and building in token sinks.
